description: #2408: dated per-file excuses for the three doc gates (check-doc-links, check-doc-style, check-phantom-command-scan). An entry is only legitimate when the real fix is a prose or product decision owned by another issue — a path/link/frontmatter one-liner gets fixed, never listed. Every entry expires; the gate goes RED the day after, so the debt cannot rot silently. Rules: doc-links | doc-style | phantom-command.

entries.reason: related: cites docs/audit/IS-ARBITER-WORTH-IT.md and docs/design/solo-developer-gate-model.md; neither exists under any prefix, so the research doc's cross-references need re-sourcing, not a path rewrite.

The skill's recipe fence instructs `arbiter invariants list`; no `invariants` command is registered in cli.ts. Shipping the command or rewriting the recipe is a self-doc correction, not a citation typo.

Step 1 of the plugin-authoring walkthrough instructs `arbiter plugin add <name>`; the command does not exist. Same ship-or-delete decision as the two website recipes and the spring-boot example README.
Public recipe instructs `arbiter plugin add`; the command does not exist. Ship it or delete the promise — a product decision.
Same `arbiter plugin add` promise as the plugin recipe; resolved by the same decision.

Example README instructs `arbiter plugin add` and cites `arbiter integrations list --recommended`; neither command is registered. Both are the plugin-registry surface awaiting the same ship-or-delete call.

The emitted governance playbook documents `arbiter audit run` and says so explicitly ("planned, not yet shipped"). Excusing the file also keeps `audit` out of the emitted-surface ledger, which would otherwise demand a row for a command that deliberately does not exist.

Cites `node scripts/check-gdpr-controls.mjs`, which is an overlay-conditional gate emitted into the CONSUMER's tree — correctly absent from arbiter's own scripts/. Do not create the file; the fix is resolving emitted-doc citations against the emitted tree.
